text:
nina_infra: kicking off security baseline for the new ap-south-2 GPU cluster (bring-up window tomorrow). main concerns: IAM bootstrapping, secrets access for node-agent, and KMS/HSM availability in-region.

raj_sre: quick note — ap-south-2 does NOT have our usual dedicated HSM pool yet. we need a fallback plan to regional KMS + perimeter controls. :warning:

mel_platform: agree. we should design an ephemeral node identity flow so nodes exchange short-lived certs and only get minimal KMS decrypt privileges. thinking: instance profile -> sts:AssumeRole -> short-lived creds -> decrypt.

zoe_security: +1 on least-priv. also require MFA for any long-lived role creation. we should add an automated policy check that blocks role policies with wildcard actions or full-resource access.

nina_infra: draft of the node bootstrap role policy I tested locally: ```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["sts:AssumeRole"],"Resource":["arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-node-init"]},
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:Decrypt"],"Resource":["arn:aws:kms:ap-south-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01"]}
  ]
}
```
This limits decrypt to the cluster KMS key.

raj_sre: can we avoid embedding the key ARN in userdata? instead use instance metadata to pick region key and call a bootstrap service that maps cluster-id -> key-arn. reduces leak surface.

mel_platform: yep — proposed flow: 1) instance boots with instance profile that only allows `sts:GetCallerIdentity` and `ec2:DescribeInstances` for self-check 2) call internal bootstrap service over mTLS 3) service checks cluster enrollment + policy 4) bootstrap service returns short-lived token allowing `kms:Decrypt` for X minutes.

provision-bot: deploy-check: bootstrap-service (v1.4.2) endpoint reachable, certs valid, HSM flag = false for ap-south-2.

zoe_security: add these automated policy checks before handoff: 
- deny iam policies with `Resource: "*"` for kms/iam/ec2 actions
- require `Condition` for `sts:AssumeRole` limiting `aws:SourceArn` to our fleet-controller
- ensure all KMS keys have `policy:Allow use only if request originates from VPC endpoint` when HSM unavailable

nina_infra: runbook snippets for validation (please run from bastion in ap-south-2):
```
# verify KMS key exists and has correct policy
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/redwood-cluster-ap-south-2 --query Policy

# check node bootstrap token retrieval
curl -v --cert /etc/boot/cert.pem https://bootstrap.internal.redwood/api/v1/token?cluster=ap-south-2

# verify role conditions
aws iam get-role --role-name redwood-node-init --query AssumeRolePolicyDocument
```

raj_sre: test plan items to pass before handoff: 
1) nodes can decrypt small secret blob (kms decrypt) within <150ms average
2) node identity flow rotates token every 10m, leak window <15m
3) automated linting rejects overly-broad IAM statements
4) failover: if KMS call fails, node should fall back to cached prefix KV (read-only) for a bounded window, not block pod start

mel_platform: cost note — HSM vs KMS per-region: HSM has steep per-hour cost and minimum commitment. For low-util regions we should default to KMS with strict network controls, and flag HSM for enterprise customers only. add these numbers to the handoff doc.

zoe_security: add a final gating checklist for security review: 
- [ ] IAM role ARNs enumerated and locked 
- [ ] KMS keys created, policies attached, key rotation scheduled 
- [ ] Bootstrap service mTLS certs rotated and in vault 
- [ ] Secrets engine path policies reviewed (no wildcard write) 
- [ ] Audit logging enabled to central SIEM for kms:Decrypt, iam:PassRole 

nina_infra: +1. can someone take ownership to run the policy linter and KMS policy audit? I'd like results by EOD.

raj_sre: taking it. I'll run linter, scan for `Resource: "*"`, and push a report. expect output: 1) list of offending policies 2) quick remediations (least-priv templates).

provision-bot: scheduled job: iam-linter -> run (target: ap-south-2 roles), ETA 2h.

mel_platform: when handing off to ops, include the fallback behavior matrix (KMS timeout -> cached read -> alert to oncall). also include `terraform import` steps for keys so ops can reconcile state.

zoe_security: last call — enforce `kms:ViaService` and `aws:SourceIp` conditions where possible; otherwise mark as security accepted risk with mitigation.

nina_infra: perfect. we'll reconvene after the linter report and the decrypt latency probe. thanks all. :pray:
